Governance within the context of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database involves the structural and strategic oversight of clinical quality indicators and organizational anchoring. The governance framework ensures that the database remains clinically relevant and methodologically sound amid changing demographic landscapes.

A key aspect of this governance is the strategic consideration of outcome metrics. The [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]] is actively evaluating the need to age-standardize all outcome indicators to account for ongoing demographic developments [^src1]. This reflects a proactive governance approach aimed at ensuring that quality measurements remain accurate and fair as the patient population ages.

Structurally, the governance and operational foundation of the database are deeply integrated with national medical societies. Specifically, the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK) is firmly anchored within the [[dansk-cardiologisk-selskab|Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab]] (DCS) [^src2]. This organizational alignment ensures that the database's governance benefits from direct oversight and endorsement by the primary professional body for cardiology in Denmark, reinforcing its authority and clinical applicability.
